methodology: Compiled from Wikipedia equipment lists (List of equipment of the Armed Forces of Ukraine) and current open-source defense reporting (news outlets, manufacturer statements, US/allied government budget and export documents). Cross-referenced against Oryx ('Attack On Europe: Documenting Ukrainian Equipment Losses') and Oryx's 'Answering the Call' list of Western equipment deliveries, to prioritize models with substantial documented service rather than obscure or single-instance donations. Western-supplied equipment generally has better-documented pricing than domestically-produced or Soviet-legacy systems -- treat unit_cost_usd as open-source estimates. Entries whose cost_confidence is 'low' rely on general open-source consensus rather than a specific citable transaction. In-service quantities and combat losses change continuously amid the ongoing war and are intentionally not included here (see Oryx for real-time loss counts).
notes_on_comparison_group: Use 'comparison_group' to match equivalent entries against russian_military_equipment.json. Not every entry has a direct counterpart (e.g. Ukraine's Magura V5 has no close Russian equivalent).

equipment.name: T-64BV
equipment.manufacturer: Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau (Soviet-era design)

unit_cost_usd.basis: Refurbishment/upgrade cost estimate; no longer newly manufactured

equipment.combat_notes: Ukraine's most numerous indigenous tank type (500+ hulls incl. variants); supplemented since 2023 by donated Leopard 2, Challenger 2, and M1 Abrams.

equipment.name: Leopard 2A6
equipment.country_of_origin: Germany (donated by Germany, Netherlands, and other operators)

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate; donated units, not purchased new

equipment.combat_notes: Among the first Western MBTs delivered to Ukraine (early 2023); older 2A4 variants also supplied by Poland, Portugal, Spain and others.

equipment.name: M1A1 Abrams

unit_cost_usd.basis: Refurbished-unit estimate; new-production packages with support run far higher ($18-24M)

equipment.combat_notes: 31 M1A1 Abrams delivered in 2023; found to be a resource-intensive platform to maintain in Ukraine's field conditions.

equipment.name: BTR-4E Bucephalus
equipment.manufacturer: Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau

unit_cost_usd.basis: Not publicly disclosed; comparable 8x8 APCs run roughly $1-2M

specifications.main_armament: BM-7 Parus remote weapon station: 30mm autocannon + optional ATGM

equipment.combat_notes: Fully indigenous Ukrainian design, in production and combat use since 2014.

equipment.name: M2A2 Bradley

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate; donated from US Army stock

specifications.main_armament: 25mm M242 Bushmaster autocannon + TOW ATGM launcher

equipment.combat_notes: Praised by Ukrainian crews for survivability; over 180 delivered starting January 2023, credited with strong loss-exchange ratios versus Russian armor.

equipment.name: BMP-2

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for a legacy design

equipment.combat_notes: Ukraine's most numerous IFV type from shared Soviet-era stockpiles, alongside captured Russian examples.

equipment.name: 2S22 Bohdana
equipment.manufacturer: Kramatorsk Heavy Duty Machine Tool Plant

unit_cost_usd.basis: Manufacturer-confirmed pricing (~EUR 2.3-2.8M), reported by Defense Express / Bild

equipment.combat_notes: Ukraine's first domestically-produced NATO-caliber self-propelled howitzer; monthly production scaled from 6 (2023) to 30+ (2026).

equipment.name: 2S1 Gvozdika

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for reactivated Soviet stock

equipment.combat_notes: Legacy Soviet-stock howitzer still fielded by Ukraine alongside Western-donated systems.

equipment.name: M777 Howitzer

unit_cost_usd.basis: US procurement estimate

equipment.combat_notes: Ultra-light titanium/aluminum howitzer, easily air-transportable; one of the first major Western artillery systems delivered to Ukraine in 2022.

equipment.name: M142 HIMARS

unit_cost_usd.basis: US Army budget line, domestic procurement (launcher only, excludes rockets)

specifications.rocket_pods: 6x MLRS rockets, or 1x ATACMS, or 2x PrSM

equipment.combat_notes: Credited with disrupting Russian ammunition depots and logistics from mid-2022 onward; direct counterpart to Tornado-S.

equipment.name: BM-21 Grad

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for the launcher vehicle

equipment.combat_notes: Still a mainstay unguided-rocket system for Ukrainian forces from shared Soviet-era stockpiles.

equipment.name: Flakpanzer Gepard

unit_cost_usd.basis: General estimate; delivered from decommissioned Bundeswehr stock plus a $118.3M US-funded reactivation/ammunition contract

equipment.combat_notes: A 1970s Cold War design that became one of Ukraine's most cost-effective weapons against Shahed/Geran drone swarms; a Ukrainian crew reported downing 10+ drones and 2 cruise missiles in a single engagement.

equipment.name: IRIS-T SLM

unit_cost_usd.basis: Per-battery cost, European defense reporting

equipment.combat_notes: Reported near-100% intercept success rate over more than 250 engagements in Ukraine since October 2022.

equipment.name: MIM-104 Patriot (PAC-3 MSE)

unit_cost_usd.basis: Cost per battery: ~$1.09B domestic (CSIS/CRS estimate) up to ~$2.5B for export configurations

pac3_mse_interceptor_usd.note: Cost per interceptor missile, purchased separately and repeatedly

specifications.targets: Ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, aircraft, drones

equipment.combat_notes: Shields Kyiv and other cities from Russian ballistic missile strikes; a $4M interceptor is often used against $20-50k drones.

equipment.name: Bayraktar TB2

unit_cost_usd.basis: Widely varying by contract; commonly cited near $5M for a full configuration

specifications.armament: Up to 4x Roketsan MAM-L / MAM-C laser-guided smart munitions

equipment.combat_notes: Became a cultural symbol of Ukrainian resistance early in the war; effectiveness declined as Russian air defenses matured.

equipment.name: Fire Point FP-1

unit_cost_usd.basis: Manufacturer-reported figure

equipment.combat_notes: Domestically-produced long-range strike drone used to hit refineries and military sites deep inside Russia.

equipment.name: Magura V5

unit_cost_usd.basis: USNI / open-source estimates

equipment.combat_notes: First uncrewed surface vessel to sink a warship in combat (Feb 2024); credited with 29+ Russian vessels sunk/damaged plus 2 aircraft and 1 helicopter shot down, driving the Black Sea Fleet from Crimea.

equipment.name: F-16AM/BM Fighting Falcon
equipment.manufacturer: Lockheed Martin (donated by Denmark, Netherlands, Norway, Belgium)

unit_cost_usd.basis: Estimated secondhand transfer value; new-build Block 70 runs $60-80M

specifications.armament: M61A1 20mm cannon, AIM-9/AIM-120 missiles, JDAM-ER, Storm Shadow/SCALP

equipment.combat_notes: Became Ukraine's principal fighter by mid-2026, replacing the aging MiG-29/Su-27 fleet; scored its first confirmed air-to-air kill (a Su-35) in July 2026.

equipment.name: MiG-29
equipment.country_of_origin: USSR legacy / donated by Poland, Slovakia

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for legacy airframes

specifications.armament: 30mm cannon + R-27/R-73 missiles; modified to carry AGM-88 HARM and JDAM-ER

equipment.combat_notes: Long-time backbone of the Ukrainian Air Force; still flying combat sorties (incl. GBU-39/HAMMER glide bombs) alongside the newer F-16 fleet as of mid-2026.

equipment.name: Su-25 Grach

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate

specifications.armament: 30mm twin-barrel cannon + rockets, bombs, guided munitions

equipment.combat_notes: Flown by Ukraine from shared Cold War stocks for frontline close air support.

equipment.name: Mi-24/Mi-35 Hind
equipment.manufacturer: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant (Soviet-era design, refurbished/donated)
equipment.country_of_origin: USSR legacy / donated by Czech Republic, Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, Croatia

unit_cost_usd.basis: Modernized/refurbished unit estimates

equipment.combat_notes: Nicknamed the 'flying tank'; still flown alongside Mi-8 in Ukraine's army aviation.

equipment.name: Mi-8

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for modernized variants

equipment.combat_notes: Overhauled and modernized Soviet-era Mi-8s form the core of Ukrainian Army Aviation's transport fleet, supplemented by donated examples.

equipment.name: FGM-148 Javelin

unit_cost_usd.basis: Cost per missile round, US budget documents

equipment.combat_notes: Became an early symbol of Ukrainian resistance ("Saint Javelin"); highly effective against Russian armor in the war's opening phase.

equipment.name: NLAW
equipment.manufacturer: Saab Bofors Dynamics / Thales Air Defence

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate, per missile

specifications.guidance: Predicted Line of Sight (PLOS) with overfly-top-attack mode

equipment.combat_notes: Lightweight, disposable, one-man-portable launcher; UK deliveries beginning January 2022 made it one of the earliest and most iconic anti-tank weapons of the war.

equipment.name: Ada-class corvette (Hetman Ivan Mazepa)

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source program cost estimate

specifications.armament: Harpoon anti-ship missiles, 76mm gun, torpedoes, VLS for future SAM integration

equipment.combat_notes: Ukraine's first modern surface combatant, built in Turkey as the planned lead ship of a rebuilt Ukrainian Navy; a second hull is being completed domestically at Okean Shipyard.
